pmp.question: A newly formed agile team is starting a product that will replace three internal tools. Team members describe the goal differently, and some think it is only a technical upgrade. What should the project manager do first?
options: Ask the team lead to write a vision statement and email it to everyone
Facilitate a vision workshop with the product owner, team and key users to co-create a product vision and measurable outcomes
Start the first sprint and let the vision emerge
Ask the sponsor to present the business case at the next all-hands meeting
pmp.explanation: A common vision is strongest when it is created together with the people who will deliver and use the product. A co-created vision builds understanding and commitment that a document alone cannot.

pmp.question: A project has stable regulatory requirements for its infrastructure work and uncertain user requirements for its customer app. Which delivery approach is most appropriate?
options: Predictive for the whole project
Agile for the whole project
A hybrid approach: predictive for the infrastructure and adaptive for the app, with integrated milestones
Whichever approach the team prefers
pmp.explanation: Tailoring the delivery approach to each component’s uncertainty and constraints is the essence of a hybrid approach. The parts must still be integrated through shared milestones and governance.

pmp.question: A new hybrid program has no clear rules for who can approve scope changes, budget changes or release decisions. What should the project manager do first?
options: Make all decisions personally to avoid delays
Work with the sponsor to define governance: decision rights, escalation paths and thresholds, and the roles of the steering committee, product owners and change control board
Let each team decide independently
Wait for the PMO to issue a policy
pmp.explanation: Governance defines how decisions are made, by whom and within which limits. Establishing it early prevents delays and conflicts later.

pmp.question: Two senior stakeholders publicly disagree in a steering meeting about project priorities. What should the project manager do?
options: Side with the more senior stakeholder
Acknowledge both views, propose a follow-up session to evaluate the options against the business case, and document the decision
Ignore the disagreement and continue the agenda
Ask the team to choose
pmp.explanation: Conflict between stakeholders should be handled respectfully and resolved with objective information. A follow-up session lets the parties work it through without derailing the meeting.

pmp.question: The product owner must choose which of four features to build next. Which approach best maximizes value?
options: Build the feature requested by the most senior stakeholder
Prioritize using value, cost of delay, risk reduction and effort—for example with weighted shortest job first
Build the easiest feature first
Build features in the order they were requested
pmp.explanation: Value-based prioritization considers economic value, urgency, risk and size. Weighted shortest job first is one common technique.

pmp.question: A change request has been approved by the change control board. What should the project manager do next?
options: Close the change request
Update the affected baselines and plans, implement the change, and communicate it to the affected stakeholders
Ask the requester to implement it
Wait for the next phase
pmp.explanation: After approval, the project manager updates the plans and baselines, manages implementation and informs stakeholders.

pmp.question: An influential operations manager says agile is “chaos” and refuses to give feedback until the product is complete. What should the project manager do?
options: Remove the manager from the stakeholder list
Show working increments in a short, focused session tied to the manager’s goals, and explain how early feedback reduces risk
Switch the project to a predictive approach
Ask HR to intervene
pmp.explanation: Engagement improves when stakeholders see value that matters to them. Demonstrating working results and explaining the benefits of early feedback builds trust.

pmp.question: Which contract type places the most cost risk on the seller?
options: Cost plus fixed fee
Time and materials
Firm fixed price
Cost plus award fee
pmp.explanation: Under a firm fixed price contract, the seller must deliver for the agreed price, so the seller bears most of the cost risk.

capm.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
capm.question: Which statement best describes a project?
options: A temporary endeavour undertaken to create a unique product, service or result
An ongoing activity that keeps the organization running from day to day
A permanent team that maintains an existing product for its whole life
A set of repeated tasks that produce the same output each month
capm.explanation: Projects are temporary and produce unique results; operations are ongoing and repetitive.

capm.question: Which project is the best fit for a predictive approach?
options: Building a bridge with fixed engineering requirements and strict regulations
Developing a new mobile app whose features are still uncertain
Exploring a new market with frequent customer feedback
Creating a prototype to test several design ideas
capm.explanation: Stable, well-defined requirements with high cost of change favour predictive approaches.

capm.question: Which project is the best fit for an adaptive approach?
options: A new customer app where needs will be discovered through user feedback
A pipeline built to a fixed engineering specification
A regulatory report with a fixed format and deadline
A building renovation with approved architectural drawings
capm.explanation: Adaptive approaches suit uncertain requirements that evolve with feedback.

capm.question: What is a main responsibility of a business analyst on a project?
options: Eliciting, analysing and communicating requirements
Approving the scope baseline and change requests
Managing the project schedule and resources
Testing the solution and fixing its defects
capm.explanation: Business analysts focus on understanding needs and defining requirements.

capm.domain: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
capm.question: What is the work breakdown structure (WBS)?
options: A hierarchical decomposition of the total scope into deliverables and work packages
A hierarchical chart of the project team showing reporting lines and roles
A bar chart that shows scheduled activities against a calendar timeline
A table of activities with their durations, dependencies and float
capm.explanation: The WBS breaks scope into manageable work packages.

capm.question: A team builds a data centre with fixed hardware requirements and a software portal whose features are uncertain. What approach is most appropriate?
options: Hybrid: predictive for the data centre, adaptive for the portal
Predictive for both, with all portal features fixed upfront
Adaptive for both, with no fixed plan for the data centre
No formal approach, because the work is mixed
capm.explanation: Different parts of a project can use different approaches.

ecba.question: Which statement best describes business analysis?
options: The practice of enabling change by defining needs and recommending solutions that deliver value
The practice of documenting system functions so developers can build what users request
The practice of controlling project scope, schedule and cost on behalf of a sponsor
The practice of testing solutions against requirements before they are released to users
ecba.explanation: Business analysis enables change by defining needs and recommending solutions that deliver value.

ecba.question: A stakeholder says, "We need a new dashboard." What should a curious business analyst do first?
options: Ask what decisions the dashboard should support and what problem it solves
Ask which charts and colours the stakeholder would like to see on it
Ask the developer how long a dashboard would take to build and test
Ask the sponsor whether there is budget available for a dashboard
ecba.explanation: Curiosity means understanding the underlying need before accepting a proposed solution.

ecba.question: What should a business analyst do before starting analysis work on a new initiative?
options: Plan the approach: activities, stakeholders, techniques and deliverables
Write a draft of the requirements so stakeholders have something to review
Choose the solution so that the analysis can focus on the right details
Prepare test cases so that requirements can be checked as they are written
ecba.explanation: Planning the business analysis approach makes the work fit the initiative.

ecba.question: In business analysis, what is a change?
options: The act of transforming in response to a need
A software release that adds new features
A decision by management to restructure
A request from a stakeholder for a solution
ecba.explanation: Change is the act of transformation in response to a need, and it is what business analysis enables.

ecba.question: Which statement is a need rather than a solution?
options: Customers wait too long for answers to simple questions
We need a chatbot to answer customer questions
We should buy new contact centre software
We should hire more contact centre staff
ecba.explanation: A need is a problem or opportunity. The others are proposed solutions.

ecba.question: What is a solution in business analysis terms?
options: A specific way of satisfying one or more needs in a context
A software product selected to replace a current system
The option with the lowest cost and the fastest delivery
The approved set of requirements for an initiative
ecba.explanation: A solution satisfies needs by resolving a problem or enabling an opportunity.

cbap.question: A project has high uncertainty and a product owner who is available every day. Which business analysis approach is MOST suitable?
options: An adaptive approach, with requirements elaborated just in time
A predictive approach, with all requirements approved upfront
A predictive approach, with a formal sign-off at each phase
An adaptive approach, with requirements frozen after the first sprint
cbap.explanation: Adaptive approaches suit uncertainty and frequent stakeholder access.

cbap.question: Before an elicitation workshop, what should the business analyst do?
options: Define the goals, agenda, participants and the materials needed
Write the final requirements so participants only need to approve them
Invite as many people as possible so that no view is missed
Ask the developers to design the solution for participants to review
cbap.explanation: Preparation sets scope, goals, logistics and participants.

cbap.question: A stakeholder asks why a particular feature is being built. Which information helps answer this?
options: Backward traceability from the feature to the requirement and business objective
Forward traceability from the feature to the test cases that verify it
The list of developers assigned to build and maintain the feature
The estimated effort and cost of building the feature in this release
cbap.explanation: Backward traceability links to origin and justification.

cbap.question: Why should the business analyst understand the current state before defining a solution?
options: It shows the root causes of the need and what must change
It shows which software vendor the organisation already uses
It shows the cost of the project that has been approved
It shows the order in which features should be released
cbap.explanation: Current state analysis explains the need in context.

cbap.question: Which model BEST shows the rules that decide a loan application outcome based on several conditions?
options: A decision table
A data flow diagram
A state diagram
A process model
cbap.explanation: Decision tables capture complex rule combinations.

cbap.question: Which item is the BEST measure of solution performance?
options: A measure tied to the business objective, such as cost per transaction
The number of features that were delivered in the last release
The number of hours the team worked during the last month
The number of user stories completed in the last iteration

itil.question: Which statement best describes a service?
options: A means of enabling value co-creation by facilitating outcomes customers want, without them managing specific costs and risks
A set of resources owned by the consumer and operated on their behalf by the provider under a fixed contract
A configuration of technology and people that the provider uses internally to run its own operations
A formal agreement that defines the targets, penalties and reporting for an outsourced activity
itil.explanation: A service enables value co-creation by facilitating outcomes for the customer while the provider takes on specific costs and risks.

itil.domain: Four dimensions of product and service management
itil.question: Which dimension covers roles, responsibilities, culture, skills and competencies?
options: Organizations and people
Information and technology
Partners and suppliers
Value streams and processes
itil.explanation: Organizations and people covers structures, roles, culture, staffing and competencies needed to create and support products and services.

itil.question: Which list contains activities of the ITIL product and service lifecycle?
options: Discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver and support
Plan, improve, engage, design, obtain, build, deliver and support
Strategy, design, transition, operation and continual service improvement
Initiate, plan, execute, monitor, control, close, review and retire
itil.explanation: The Version 5 lifecycle describes eight activities from discovering needs to supporting the product or service in use.

itil.question: Which guiding principle recommends reusing existing services, processes and tools where possible?
options: Start where you are
Keep it simple and practical
Optimize and automate
Focus on value
itil.explanation: Start where you are means assessing what already exists, through direct observation, before building something new.

itil.question: What is a value stream?
options: A series of steps an organization takes to create and deliver products and services
A catalogue of all the services an organization offers to its consumer groups
A set of agreed targets for the performance of a service over a fixed period
A model of how information flows between the organization's technical systems
itil.explanation: A value stream is the end-to-end set of steps that turns demand into value for a consumer.

itil.question: Which approach to using AI in service management is consistent with ITIL guidance?
options: Use AI to support people and decisions, with governance, human accountability and attention to risk
Let AI make routine decisions without oversight so that staff can focus on strategic work
Use AI only where it can fully replace human roles, to maximize the reduction in costs
Avoid AI in service management until the technology is proven to be completely accurate
itil.explanation: AI can add value to products and services, but it needs governance, transparency and human accountability.
